t: 天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福
r: tiān yǒu bù cè fēng yún, rén yǒu dàn xī huò fú
mean: disaster can strike anyone suddenly and without warning
lit: the sky has wind and clouds no one can predict; people have fortune and disaster between morning and night

use.how: Said as a whole sentence, often with a sigh, after someone suffers a sudden accident, illness or loss, or to argue for being prepared: 真是天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福。

near.diff: 屋漏偏逢连夜雨 is one misfortune piling onto another; 天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福 says a misfortune can strike out of the blue.

cue: A fit, healthy neighbour in his forties was rushed to hospital last night with a stroke. Everyone in the building sighs that nobody could have seen it coming.

ctx.s: 谁也想不到他会突然生病，真是{天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福}。
ctx.en: Nobody imagined he would suddenly fall ill. You really never know what's coming.

ctx.s: 昨天还好好的，今天就出了车祸，唉，{天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福}啊。
ctx.en: He was perfectly fine yesterday, and today he's had a car accident. Sigh, disaster can strike anyone at any time.

ctx.s: {天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福}，买份保险总是有备无患。
ctx.en: Misfortune can come without warning, so taking out insurance is always a sensible precaution.

ctx.s: 奶奶常说：“{天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福}，一家人在一起的日子要珍惜。”
ctx.en: Grandma always says: "You never know what tomorrow brings, so treasure the days the family is together."

ctx.s: 听说老同学的工厂一夜之间被大火烧光了，大家都感叹{天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福}。
ctx.en: When we heard an old classmate's factory had burned down overnight, we all sighed at how suddenly disaster can strike.

ctx.s: 正因为{天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福}，他一直坚持在银行里留一笔应急的钱。
ctx.en: It is precisely because misfortune can come out of nowhere that he always keeps some emergency money in the bank.

bad.s: 明天可能会下雨，{天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福}，记得带伞。
bad.en: (meant: it may rain tomorrow, so remember your umbrella)
bad.why: Despite the wind and clouds, it is not about the weather: it is about sudden misfortune in people's lives.

bad.s: 他考试前一点儿也没复习，结果没及格，真是{天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福}。
bad.en: (meant: he didn't study at all and failed)
bad.why: Failing after not studying was entirely foreseeable; the saying is only for blows that nobody could have predicted.

mean: fortunes rise and fall; everyone gets a turn at the top
lit: good feng shui turns round from one house to the next

use.how: Said as a comment when the one who used to be on top falls and another rises, often with a grin by the new winner or as a warning: 别太得意，风水轮流转。

near.diff: 长江后浪推前浪 is a new generation overtaking the old for good; 风水轮流转 is luck changing hands, so the one now down may rise again.

cue: For years your team came last in the office quiz while another team always won. This year you win and they come last. What do you say, grinning?

ctx.s: 去年他们赢了我们，今年我们赢回来了，{风水轮流转}嘛。
ctx.en: They beat us last year and this year we beat them back. Everyone gets their turn.

ctx.s: 以前总是我求他帮忙，现在轮到他来求我了，真是{风水轮流转}。
ctx.en: I used to be the one asking him for favours, and now he's asking me. The tables really have turned.

ctx.s: 别太得意，{风水轮流转}，说不定明年就轮到别人了。
ctx.en: Don't get too cocky. Luck moves on, and next year it may be someone else's turn.

ctx.s: 这家小店从前没什么人去，现在门口天天排队，老板笑着说：“{风水轮流转}啊！”
ctx.en: Hardly anyone used to go to this little shop; now there's a queue every day. The owner laughs: "It's our turn now!"

ctx.s: 几年前这个行业最赚钱，现在却不景气，{风水轮流转}，谁也说不准。
ctx.en: A few years ago this was the most profitable industry; now it's in a slump. Fortunes come and go, and nobody can say what's next.

ctx.s: 打牌连输了十几把，他终于赢了一把，高兴地喊道：“{风水轮流转}，总算到我了！”
ctx.en: After losing more than ten hands in a row he finally won one and shouted: "Luck comes round, and at last it's my turn!"

bad.s: 我们家每年都{风水轮流转}，把家具的位置换一换。
bad.en: (meant: every year our family rearranges the furniture for good feng shui)
bad.why: It is not about arranging a home by feng shui; it says fortune passes from one person or group to another.

bad.s: 他从小到大一直是班里第一名，真是{风水轮流转}。
bad.en: (meant: he has always been top of the class)
bad.why: The saying describes the top place changing hands; someone who stays on top is the very opposite.

r: bù dào huáng hé xīn bù sǐ
mean: to refuse to give up until every hope is gone
lit: until he reaches the Yellow River, his heart won't die

use.how: Describes a stubborn person who keeps on with a hopeless plan until they hit the dead end themselves; often 他这个人不到黄河心不死。 Usually exasperated, not admiring.

near.diff: 不见棺材不落泪 is refusing to admit fault or defeat until faced with hard proof; 不到黄河心不死 is refusing to drop a hope or plan.
死马当活马医 is trying a last remedy while knowing it is hopeless; 不到黄河心不死 is refusing to accept it is hopeless at all.

cue: Every publisher has turned down your friend's novel and everyone tells him to stop, but he insists on sending it to the last two anyway. How do you describe him, with a sigh?

ctx.s: 他这个人{不到黄河心不死}，劝也没用。
ctx.en: He's the type who won't give up till he hits a brick wall. There's no point trying to talk him out of it.

ctx.s: 都被拒绝三次了，你还要去？真是{不到黄河心不死}。
ctx.en: You've been turned down three times and you're still going? You just won't give up until there's no hope left.

ctx.s: 妈妈叹气说：“这孩子{不到黄河心不死}，让他自己去碰碰钉子吧。”
ctx.en: Mum sighed: "This child won't listen until he's run into the wall himself. Let him find out the hard way."

ctx.s: 明知道这个项目没希望了，老板还是{不到黄河心不死}，又投了一笔钱。
ctx.en: Everyone knew the project was hopeless, but the boss refused to give up and put in more money.

ctx.s: 已经连着落榜两次了，他还是{不到黄河心不死}，今年又报了名。
ctx.en: He has already failed the entrance exam twice, but he still won't give up: he has signed up again this year.

ctx.s: 有些人{不到黄河心不死}，非得亲身吃了亏才会回头。
ctx.en: Some people won't give up until all hope is gone; they only turn back after they've been burned themselves.

bad.s: 他学习{不到黄河心不死}，每天都努力到深夜，真让人佩服。
bad.en: (meant: he is admirably persistent in his studies)
bad.why: It mocks stubbornness in a lost cause; it is not praise for hard work or perseverance.

bad.s: 他遇到一点儿困难就放弃了，真是{不到黄河心不死}。
bad.en: (meant: he gives up at the first difficulty)
bad.why: It describes someone who refuses to give up even when it is hopeless, the opposite of quitting easily.

r: hǎo mǎ bù chī huí tóu cǎo
mean: a person with pride doesn't go back to what they have left
lit: a good horse doesn't turn back to eat the grass it has passed

use.how: Said about returning to a former partner, employer or place one chose to leave, as a reason not to go back: 我不会回去的，好马不吃回头草。

near.diff: 天涯何处无芳草 comforts someone after a breakup that others are out there; 好马不吃回头草 says going back would be beneath you.

cue: Six months after you quit, your old boss phones and offers you your job back at the same pay. You turn it down with your pride intact. What do you say?

ctx.s: 我已经辞职了，{好马不吃回头草}，不会再回去。
ctx.en: I've already resigned. I don't go back to what I've left, so I won't return.

ctx.s: 前男友想跟她复合，她只回了一句：“{好马不吃回头草}。”
ctx.en: Her ex wanted to get back together, and she replied with a single line: "I don't go backwards."

ctx.s: 分手以后，朋友们都劝她{好马不吃回头草}，别再联系那个人了。
ctx.en: After the breakup her friends all told her not to go back to him and to stop contacting him.

ctx.s: 老公司请他回去当经理，他有点犹豫：{好马不吃回头草}，可条件确实不错。
ctx.en: His old company asked him back as a manager. He hesitated: a proud man doesn't go back, but the offer really was good.

ctx.s: 谁说{好马不吃回头草}？只要那份工作适合你，回去又怎么样？
ctx.en: Who says you can never go back? If the job suits you, what's wrong with returning?

ctx.s: 当年他一气之下离开了家乡的工厂，因为{好马不吃回头草}，再苦也没回去过。
ctx.en: Years ago he walked out of his hometown factory in anger, and out of pride he never went back, however hard things got.

bad.s: 这家饭馆很好吃，可我{好马不吃回头草}，下次想换一家试试。
bad.en: (meant: I like to try a new restaurant each time)
bad.why: It is about the pride of not returning to a person or job you left, not about liking variety.

bad.s: 他犯了大错，被公司开除了，真是{好马不吃回头草}。
bad.en: (meant: he made a big mistake and was fired)
bad.why: It describes someone's own proud choice not to go back, not being thrown out by others.

mean: to punish one person as a warning to all the others
lit: to kill a chicken for the monkeys to watch

use.how: Said about someone in authority who makes an example of one person; often used to see through the motive: 这是杀鸡给猴看。

near.diff: 枪打出头鸟 says whoever stands out gets attacked first; 杀鸡给猴看 is about the punisher's aim of frightening everyone else.

cue: Thirty students copied the same homework, but the teacher punished only one of them, loudly and in front of the whole class, so the rest would get the message. What was the teacher doing?

ctx.s: 老师当着全班的面批评他，其实是{杀鸡给猴看}。
ctx.en: The teacher criticised him in front of the whole class, but really it was a warning to everyone else.

ctx.s: 公司开除了一个经常迟到的员工，大家都明白这是{杀鸡给猴看}。
ctx.en: The company fired one employee who was often late, and everyone understood it was meant as a warning to the rest of us.

ctx.s: 为什么只罚我一个人？不就是想{杀鸡给猴看}吗？
ctx.en: Why punish only me? Isn't it just to make an example of me?

ctx.s: 好几个人一起作弊，校长却只处分了班长，大家私下说这是{杀鸡给猴看}。
ctx.en: Several students cheated together, but the head only disciplined the class monitor. Privately everyone said he was making an example of him.

ctx.s: 教练让迟到的主力坐了一整场替补席，就是要{杀鸡给猴看}。
ctx.en: The coach kept the star player who'd turned up late on the bench for the whole match, precisely to send a message to the others.

ctx.s: 市场管理部门重罚了一家卖假货的商店，{杀鸡给猴看}，其他商家马上老实了。
ctx.en: The market regulators fined one shop selling fakes heavily as an example, and the other sellers fell into line at once.

bad.s: 老板奖励了最努力的员工，这是{杀鸡给猴看}，鼓励大家向他学习。
bad.en: (meant: the boss rewarded the hardest worker to encourage everyone)
bad.why: It is about punishing one person to frighten others, never about rewarding someone as a good example.

bad.s: 老师把全班同学都罚站了，真是{杀鸡给猴看}。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher punished the whole class)
bad.why: The point is punishing just one so the others take warning; punishing everybody is not making an example.

r: yú yǔ xióng zhǎng bù kě jiān dé
mean: you can't have both of two good things; you must choose
lit: fish and bear's paw cannot both be had

story.text: Mencius said: fish is something I want, and bear's paw, a great delicacy, is also something I want; if I cannot have both, I will give up the fish and take the bear's paw. In the same way, life is something I want and righteousness is also something I want; if I cannot have both, I will give up life and choose righteousness.

use.how: Said as a comment when someone wants two attractive things that exclude each other; also 鱼和熊掌不可兼得. Often followed by advice to choose: 你得自己选。

near.diff: 两全其美 describes a solution that satisfies both sides at once; 鱼与熊掌不可兼得 says no such solution exists here.

cue: Your friend has two offers: a well-paid job in a distant city, or a modest one near her family. She keeps hoping to have both. What do you tell her?

ctx.s: 又想要高工资又想要轻松，{鱼与熊掌不可兼得}啊。
ctx.en: You want a high salary and an easy job too? You can't have it both ways.

ctx.s: 大城市机会多，小城市生活舒服，{鱼与熊掌不可兼得}，你得自己选。
ctx.en: A big city has more opportunities and a small town is more comfortable. You can't have both, so you'll have to choose.

ctx.s: “我既想出国读书，又不想离开家人。”“{鱼与熊掌不可兼得}，总要放弃一个。”
ctx.en: "I want to study abroad, but I don't want to leave my family." "You can't have both; you'll have to give one up."

ctx.s: 这款手机拍照很好，电池却不耐用，看来{鱼与熊掌不可兼得}。
ctx.en: This phone takes great photos but the battery doesn't last. It seems you can't have both.

ctx.s: 她最后选择留在家里照顾孩子，暂时放下了事业，毕竟{鱼与熊掌不可兼得}。
ctx.en: In the end she chose to stay home with the children and put her career on hold. After all, you can't have everything.

ctx.s: 在自由和稳定之间，很多年轻人觉得{鱼与熊掌不可兼得}。
ctx.en: Between freedom and security, many young people feel they can't have both.

bad.s: 他既有钱又有时间，真是{鱼与熊掌不可兼得}。
bad.en: (meant: he is lucky enough to have both money and time)
bad.why: The saying denies that you can have both; it cannot describe someone who actually has both.

bad.s: 他又懒又粗心，真是{鱼与熊掌不可兼得}。
bad.en: (meant: he has two faults at once)
bad.why: It is about having to choose between two good things, not about someone having two bad qualities.

r: péi le fū rén yòu zhé bīng
mean: to lose twice over when one's own scheme backfires
lit: to lose the lady and lose the soldiers as well

story.text: Zhou Yu of Wu planned to lure Liu Bei to Wu with a false offer of marriage to Sun Quan's sister and hold him until Jingzhou was handed over. Zhuge Liang saw through it; the bride's mother, the dowager of Wu, took a liking to Liu Bei, and the marriage became real. Liu Bei then slipped away with his bride, Zhou Yu's pursuing troops were beaten, and Zhuge Liang's soldiers jeered: Zhou Yu's brilliant plan to secure the realm has lost him the lady and his soldiers too.

use.how: Used as a predicate or after 真是 / 落得个 about someone whose scheme to gain something ends in a double loss; often mocking: 结果赔了夫人又折兵。

near.diff: Both are about a scheme backfiring; 偷鸡不成蚀把米 is a small loss from a petty trick, 赔了夫人又折兵 a heavier double loss, often from a clever plan.
竹篮打水一场空 is effort that yields nothing; 赔了夫人又折兵 is a scheme that leaves you worse off than before, twice over.

cue: To win a contract, a company slashed its prices far below cost. It still lost the contract, and the price war left it with huge losses. How do people mock the result?

ctx.s: 他本想借合作把对手挤走，结果客户丢了，合伙人也走了，{赔了夫人又折兵}。
ctx.en: He planned to use the partnership to squeeze out his rival; instead he lost his clients and his partner walked out too. A double loss.

ctx.s: 为了省钱买了便宜货，没用几天就坏了，修又花了一大笔，真是{赔了夫人又折兵}。
ctx.en: I bought the cheap one to save money; it broke within days and the repair cost a fortune. I lost twice over.

ctx.s: “你不是托人走后门了吗？”“别提了，礼也送了，事也没办成，{赔了夫人又折兵}。”
ctx.en: "Didn't you pull some strings?" "Don't ask. I gave the gifts and still got nothing done. Lost on both ends."

ctx.s: 那家公司想靠降价挤走对手，结果对手没走，自己倒亏了一大笔，{赔了夫人又折兵}。
ctx.en: The company tried to drive its rival out with price cuts, but the rival stayed and it lost a fortune instead: a scheme that backfired twice.

ctx.s: 他装病想逃掉考试，被老师发现后不但要补考，还挨了处分，{赔了夫人又折兵}。
ctx.en: He faked illness to get out of the exam; when the teacher found out, he had to resit it and was disciplined as well. A double loss.

ctx.s: 有人借钱炒股想赚快钱，最后本钱利息全赔进去，落得个{赔了夫人又折兵}。
ctx.en: Some people borrow money to play the stock market for quick gains, and end up losing both the capital and the interest: their scheme costs them twice.

bad.s: 他出了车祸，人受了伤，车也撞坏了，真是{赔了夫人又折兵}。
bad.en: (meant: he was injured and his car was wrecked in an accident)
bad.why: An accident is bad luck, not one's own scheme backfiring; the saying always blames a plan that went wrong.

bad.s: 他去年离了婚，今年又丢了工作，{赔了夫人又折兵}。
bad.en: (meant: he lost his wife and then his job)
bad.why: The lady comes from the story; the saying is about a scheme that backfires, not literally losing a wife.

r: zhú lán dǎ shuǐ yī chǎng kōng
mean: all one's efforts come to nothing in the end
lit: drawing water with a bamboo basket: all for nothing

use.how: Describes effort, time or hope that ended with nothing to show for it; often after 结果, 到头来 or 最后: 忙了半天，到头来竹篮打水一场空。

near.diff: 赔了夫人又折兵 is a scheme that backfires and costs you twice; 竹篮打水一场空 is simply effort that yields nothing.

cue: A student prepared for months for a scholarship exam, only to find out on the day that her application had never been registered. How does she describe all that work?

ctx.s: 忙了一整年，最后{竹篮打水一场空}。
ctx.en: A whole year of hard work, and in the end it all came to nothing.

ctx.s: 如果方法不对，再努力也是{竹篮打水一场空}。
ctx.en: If your method is wrong, however hard you try, it's all wasted effort.

ctx.s: “你追了她三年，结果呢？”“别提了，{竹篮打水一场空}。”
ctx.en: "You chased her for three years. So what happened?" "Don't ask. All for nothing."

ctx.s: 他辛辛苦苦存了好几年的钱，一下子全被骗走了，到头来{竹篮打水一场空}。
ctx.en: He'd scrimped and saved for years, and then lost it all at once to a scam. All those years came to nothing.

ctx.s: 文件没保存，电脑突然死机了，几天的工夫{竹篮打水一场空}。
ctx.en: I hadn't saved the file and the computer suddenly crashed. Days of work, gone for nothing.

ctx.s: 球队拼了整整九十分钟，却在最后一刻被对手进球，所有努力{竹篮打水一场空}。
ctx.en: The team fought for the full ninety minutes, only to concede in the last moment. All that effort came to nothing.

bad.s: 孩子们都搬走了，家里{竹篮打水一场空}。
bad.en: (meant: the children have moved out and the house feels empty)
bad.why: The emptiness is of wasted effort, not of an empty house or loneliness.

bad.s: 这次考试我根本没复习，所以{竹篮打水一场空}。
bad.en: (meant: I didn't study at all, so I failed)
bad.why: It needs real effort that was wasted; with no effort put in, there was nothing to come to nothing.

r: rén bǐ rén, qì sǐ rén
mean: comparing yourself with others only makes you miserable
lit: comparing person with person makes a person furious

use.how: Said as a whole sentence, ruefully or jokingly, after comparing oneself with someone luckier, or to tell someone to stop comparing: 别比了，人比人，气死人。

near.diff: 山外有山，人外有人 is a call to stay modest because someone is always better; 人比人，气死人 is about the misery comparison brings.

cue: Your old roommate has just posted photos of her new house and her promotion, while you are still renting a shared flat. You put down your phone and sigh.

ctx.s: 别老跟别人比了，{人比人，气死人}。
ctx.en: Stop comparing yourself with other people all the time. It'll only make you miserable.

ctx.s: 同样是毕业五年，他已经买了房，我还在租房，真是{人比人，气死人}。
ctx.en: We both graduated five years ago; he's bought a flat and I'm still renting. Comparing just drives you mad.

ctx.s: “你看人家孩子，又考了第一。”“妈，{人比人，气死人}，您就别比了。”
ctx.en: "Look at their kid, top of the class again." "Mum, comparing only upsets everyone. Please stop."

ctx.s: 哥哥吃多少都不胖，我喝口水都长肉，{人比人，气死人}啊！
ctx.en: My brother can eat anything and never gains weight, while I put on pounds just drinking water. Life's so unfair when you compare!

ctx.s: 朋友圈里人人都在旅游，她看了一会儿就关了手机，心想：{人比人，气死人}。
ctx.en: Everyone on her social feed seemed to be on holiday. After a while she switched off her phone, thinking: comparing only makes you miserable.

ctx.s: 幸福是自己的感觉，{人比人，气死人}，过好自己的日子就行了。
ctx.en: Happiness is about how you feel yourself. Comparing only brings misery, so just live your own life well.

bad.s: 他们俩在操场上比赛谁跑得快，{人比人，气死人}。
bad.en: (meant: the two of them raced each other on the sports field)
bad.why: It is not about a contest between people; it is about feeling bad when you measure your own lot against someone else's.

bad.s: 他说话太难听了，{人比人，气死人}。
bad.en: (meant: what he said was so rude it made me furious)
bad.why: The anger comes from comparing yourself with others, not from someone's rude words.

r: yǎn bù jiàn, xīn bù fán
mean: what you don't see can't upset you
lit: if the eyes don't see it, the heart isn't annoyed

use.how: Said as a reason for deliberately not looking at something irritating you cannot change: shutting a door, leaving, deleting a contact: 我干脆不看了，眼不见，心不烦。

near.diff: 眼不见为净 is often about ignoring something dirty or unpleasant you'd rather not know about; 眼不见，心不烦 is about avoiding irritation.

cue: Your teenage son's bedroom is a disaster and nagging hasn't helped, so you simply keep his door closed and stop going in. Why?

ctx.s: 他的房间太乱了，我干脆把门关上，{眼不见，心不烦}。
ctx.en: His room is such a mess that I just shut the door. What I don't see can't annoy me.

ctx.s: “你怎么把他的微信删了？”“{眼不见，心不烦}嘛。”
ctx.en: "Why did you delete him from WeChat?" "If I can't see his posts, they can't annoy me."

ctx.s: 孩子打游戏我也管不了，就出门散步去了，{眼不见，心不烦}。
ctx.en: I can't stop the kids gaming anyway, so I went out for a walk. What I don't see can't bother me.

ctx.s: 股票跌得厉害，他索性把软件卸载了，{眼不见，心不烦}。
ctx.en: His shares were plunging, so he simply deleted the app. If he couldn't see it, it couldn't upset him.

ctx.s: 搬出合租房以后，再也不用看室友把脏碗堆在水池里，真是{眼不见，心不烦}。
ctx.en: Since I moved out of the shared flat, I no longer have to watch my flatmate pile dirty dishes in the sink. What a relief not to see it.

ctx.s: 她知道丈夫抽烟改不了，只要求他去阳台抽，{眼不见，心不烦}。
ctx.en: She knew her husband would never quit smoking, so she just asked him to do it on the balcony, where she wouldn't have to see it.

bad.s: 我眼睛不好，看不清黑板，{眼不见，心不烦}。
bad.en: (meant: my eyesight is poor and I can't see the board, which worries me)
bad.why: It is not about poor eyesight; it means choosing not to look at something so that it stops annoying you.

bad.s: 他一天没见到女朋友就特别想她，真是{眼不见，心不烦}。
bad.en: (meant: when he doesn't see his girlfriend he misses her)
bad.why: It says not seeing something stops it bothering you; missing someone you can't see is the opposite feeling.
